_comment: Small asks pinned to the notice board, a few each morning, drawn from the world seed so a seed always posts the same ones. 'n' is a [min, max] count. Reward is the item's worth times 1.6, plus a little; affection goes to whoever asked. 'when' uses the rule language. Text is in the asker's voice: one opinion per note.

templates.text: Beets for the pot. Proper ones. The ones with opinions.
Tea for the counter. Barnaby says he doesn't want any. Barnaby is lying.
One stew, for old Fen on the dock, who won't come in and won't say why. Don't tell him it's from me.
SALT. From Sallow. Do you know what salt does to a beet? Bring some and I'll show you.
Salted beets, for the store jars. I've counted the jars. I've counted them twice.
Pipe. Any length. Leave it by the annex door.
Wire. Copper if it's copper. Don't ask what for.
Brass. The good kind. The kind that still rings.
One pot of seal gum. The valve's weeping. It's allowed to. I'd rather it didn't.
Crew cable for the lift. Spare. You never want to need spare.
WANTED: glowglass, clear, unchipped. Paying fair. Paying exactly fair. — O.
WANTED: blackstone by the bucket. The Exchange is not a charity. It is, however, buying.
WANTED: thermal ore. Warm to the touch. Keep it away from the ledgers.
WANTED: bellcap, two. A gift for someone. Not you. Don't look at me like that.
WANTED: ember resin. Page forty of the ledger says we used to export it. I'd like page forty to be true again.
Moss fibre for the frames. Bring it gently. It notices.
Fern spores, if the Reach will spare them. Ask first. I mean it.
Fertiliser. The beds are hungry and so, frankly, am I.
Filter pads for the children's room. The damp is in. Don't make a fuss about it, just bring them.
One tincture, spare, for the shelf. The shelf is where hope goes to wait.
Sulfur. ... Tasty. ... Knappers say thank you in advance. Saves time.
Beets. ... For the crunch. ... Do not tell Mags. She will want to talk about it.
Brass. ... Not to eat. ... Mostly.
Can somebody send stew down on the cage. Wren says hers was better. Wren has never made stew. — P.
Wire for the pumps please. Also what is a cloud. — Pell, Sallow
Tea, for the pump hall. I sit there in the mornings now. It's warmer than it used to be. — P.
Another tincture, if you can. I'm not dying, I'm just making sure. Tell B nothing. — W.
Pipe! Lots! I'm building something and I'm not telling Barnaby what until it works. — W.
Sorry to ask. Filter pads, for the lower hall. Sorry. The old ones are, sorry, they're very old. — Tolley
Brass, if nobody else needs it. If somebody else needs it, give it to them. Sorry. — T.
